title: Canonical truncations and H^q(-)[-q] descend to functors on D(A), with i_q, j_q natural
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with derived category $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and for $q\in\mathbf Z$ let $\tau_{\leq q}$ be the canonical truncation of complexes ($(\tau_{\leq q}K)^r=K^r$ for $r<q$, $\Ker d^q_K$ for $r=q$, $0$ for $r>q$), a functor on cochain complexes, $H^q(-)[-q]$ the functor $K\mapsto$ (the complex with $H^q(K)$ in degree $q$, $0$ elsewhere), $i_q:\tau_{\leq q-1}\to\tau_{\leq q}$ the inclusion and $j_q:\tau_{\leq q}\to H^q(-)[-q]$ the projection $\Ker d^q\to H^q$ in degree $q$, natural transformations of functors on complexes. Then: (a) if $s:K\to L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so are $\tau_{\leq q}s$ (indeed $H^r(\tau_{\leq q}K)=H^r(K)$ for $r\le q$ and $0$ for $r>q$, naturally) and $H^q(s)[-q]$; (b) hence there are functors $\tau_{\leq q},\ H^q(-)[-q]:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$, unique up to unique isomorphism, with specified natural isomorphisms $\tau_{\leq q}\circ Q\cong Q\circ\tau_{\leq q}$ and $H^q(-)[-q]\circ Q\cong Q\circ H^q(-)[-q]$ (equalities when $D(\mathcal A)$ is constructed as a category of fractions), and unique natural transformations $i_q:\tau_{\leq q-1}\to\tau_{\leq q}$, $j_q:\tau_{\leq q}\to H^q(-)[-q]$ of functors on $D(\mathcal A)$ whose composites with $Q$ are $Q(i_q)$, $Q(j_q)$ (up to these isomorphisms). In particular a morphism $f:K\to L$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ between complexes $K,L$ gives morphisms $\tau_{\leq q}f$, $\tau_{\leq q-1}f$, $H^q(f)[-q]$ with $\tau_{\leq q}f\circ i_q=i_q\circ\tau_{\leq q-1}f$ and $H^q(f)[-q]\circ j_q=j_q\circ\tau_{\leq q}f$, and when $f=Q(\phi)$ for a morphism of complexes $\phi$ these are, up to these isomorphisms, the images under $Q$ of $\tau_{\leq q}\phi$, $\tau_{\leq q-1}\phi$, $H^q(\phi)[-q]$.

source.place: Remark 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, line 4076, 'canonical truncation functors'); the descent to D(A) by the universal property of the localization, Definition 05RU / Section 05RR; homology.tex Section 0118 (the cohomology of tau_{<=n}, line 3612ff.)

proof.text: **Step 1 ((a) for $\tau_{\leq q}$).** Let $s:K\to L$ be a quasi-isomorphism. The morphism $\tau_{\leq q}s$ is the restriction of $s$ to the subcomplexes ($s^r$ for $r<q$, the map $\Ker d^q_K\to\Ker d^q_L$ induced by $s^q$, $0$ for $r>q$), so $c_{q,L}\circ\tau_{\leq q}s=s\circ c_{q,K}$ for the inclusions $c_q:\tau_{\leq q}\to\mathrm{id}$, and $H^r(c_{q,L})\circ H^r(\tau_{\leq q}s)=H^r(s)\circ H^r(c_{q,K})$ by functoriality of $H^r$. For $r\le q$, $H^r(c_{q,K})$ and $H^r(c_{q,L})$ are isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology] and $H^r(s)$ is one by hypothesis, so $H^r(\tau_{\leq q}s)=H^r(c_{q,L})^{-1}H^r(s)H^r(c_{q,K})$ is an isomorphism. For $r>q$, $H^r(\tau_{\leq q}K)=H^r(\tau_{\leq q}L)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], and a morphism between zero objects is an isomorphism. So $\tau_{\leq q}s$ is a quasi-isomorphism; the same with $q-1$ for $\tau_{\leq q-1}s$. (Mathlib: `CochainComplex.quasiIso_truncLEMap_iff`, Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/Embedding/CochainComplex.lean:305.)

source.place: Homology, Section 12.15 (Tag 0118, section-truncations), canonical truncation tau_{<=n}A^bullet for cochain complexes, lines 3777-3804

proof.text: **Step 2 ((a) for $H^q(-)[-q]$).** For a quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to L$, $H^q(s)[-q]:H^q(K)[-q]\to H^q(L)[-q]$ is the morphism of complexes whose component in degree $q$ is $H^q(s)$ and whose other components are maps between zero objects. $H^q(s)$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis, so every component is an isomorphism, and the componentwise inverses (they commute with the zero differentials) form an inverse morphism of complexes: $H^q(s)[-q]$ is an isomorphism of complexes, hence a quasi-isomorphism, since each functor $H^r$ sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Homology, Section 12.15 (Tag 0118, section-truncations), canonical truncation tau_{<=n}A^bullet for cochain complexes, lines 3777-3804

proof.text: **Step 3 (naturality on complexes).** $i_q:\tau_{\leq q-1}\to\tau_{\leq q}$ and $j_q:\tau_{\leq q}\to H^q(-)[-q]$ are natural transformations of functors on cochain complexes: for $\phi:K\to L$, $(\tau_{\leq q-1}\phi,\tau_{\leq q}\phi)$ is part of a morphism of short exact sequences, so $\tau_{\leq q}\phi\circ i_{q,K}=i_{q,L}\circ\tau_{\leq q-1}\phi$, and $j_q=\bar j_q\circ p_q$ with $H^q(\phi)[-q]\circ\bar j_{q,K}=\bar j_{q,L}\circ M_q(\phi)$ and $M_q(\phi)\circ p_{q,K}=p_{q,L}\circ\tau_{\leq q}\phi$, whence $H^q(\phi)[-q]\circ j_{q,K}=j_{q,L}\circ\tau_{\leq q}\phi$ [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-step-ses] (c). (Degreewise: in degree $q$ the projection $\Ker d^q_K\to H^q(K)$ followed by $H^q(\phi)$ is the class of $\phi^q$ restricted to cycles.)

source.place: Homology, Section 12.15 (Tag 0118, section-truncations), canonical truncation tau_{<=n}A^bullet for cochain complexes, lines 3777-3804

proof.text: **Step 4 ((b) the functors).** $Q$ sends quasi-isomorphisms to isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so by Steps 1 and 2 the functors $Q\circ\tau_{\leq q}$, $Q\circ\tau_{\leq q-1}$ and $Q\circ H^q(-)[-q]:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ invert the quasi-isomorphisms. Since $Q$ is the localization at the quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives functors $\tau_{\leq q},\tau_{\leq q-1},H^q(-)[-q]:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ with natural isomorphisms $\phi:\tau_{\leq q}\circ Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\circ\tau_{\leq q}$ etc. (equalities for the category of fractions, Stacks 04VG (3)), and by part (2) these functors are unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the $\phi$'s.

source.place: Categories, Lemma 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization) (3); D(A) as localization: derived.tex Section 05RR, Definition 05RU

proof.text: **Step 5 ((b) the transformations).** Whiskering the natural transformations of Step 3 with $Q$ gives natural transformations $Q i_q:Q\circ\tau_{\leq q-1}\to Q\circ\tau_{\leq q}$ and $Q j_q:Q\circ\tau_{\leq q}\to Q\circ H^q(-)[-q]$ between functors inverting quasi-isomorphisms. By part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], applied with the functors and isomorphisms $\phi$ of Step 4, there are unique natural transformations $i_q:\tau_{\leq q-1}\to\tau_{\leq q}$ and $j_q:\tau_{\leq q}\to H^q(-)[-q]$ of functors on $D(\mathcal A)$ with $i_{q,QK}=\phi^{-1}\circ Q(i_{q,K})\circ\phi$ and $j_{q,QK}=\phi^{-1}\circ Q(j_{q,K})\circ\phi$ for every complex $K$; this is the statement that their composites with $Q$ are $Q(i_q)$, $Q(j_q)$ up to the $\phi$'s.

source.place: Categories, Lemma 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization) (3); D(A) as localization: derived.tex Section 05RR, Definition 05RU

proof.text: **Step 6 (the consequences for a morphism $f$).** For a morphism $f:K\to L$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ put $\tau_{\leq q}f$, $\tau_{\leq q-1}f$, $H^q(f)[-q]$ for the images of $f$ under the functors of Step 4. The two identities $\tau_{\leq q}f\circ i_{q,K}=i_{q,L}\circ\tau_{\leq q-1}f$ and $H^q(f)[-q]\circ j_{q,K}=j_{q,L}\circ\tau_{\leq q}f$ are the naturality squares of the transformations of Step 5 at $f$. If $f=Q(\phi)$, naturality of the isomorphism $\phi:\tau_{\leq q}\circ Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\circ\tau_{\leq q}$ of Step 4 at $\phi$ gives $\tau_{\leq q}(Q\phi)=\phi_L^{-1}\circ Q(\tau_{\leq q}\phi)\circ\phi_K$, and likewise for $\tau_{\leq q-1}$ and $H^q(-)[-q]$.

source.place: Categories, Lemma 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization) (3); D(A) as localization: derived.tex Section 05RR, Definition 05RU

split_report.summary: Not a leaf: Mathlib has clause (a) for tau (CochainComplex.quasiIso_truncLEMap_iff) and the localization universal property (Localization.lift/fac/liftNatTrans/natTrans_ext), and the t-structure truncation t.truncLE on DerivedCategory, but no complex-level i_q, j_q and no isomorphism between Q ⋙ t.truncLE n and truncLE ⋙ Q (searched with LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep). Split in 6 steps: (a) for tau from lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology (natural comparison by c_q), (a) for H^q[-q] elementary (componentwise isomorphism), naturality of i_q, j_q on complexes from lem-weil-pbc-truncation-step-ses (c), descent of functors and transformations by the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property (Stacks 04VG (3); Mathlib Localization.lift, liftNatTrans), and the consequences for a morphism f as naturality squares. Statement corrected in a detail: tau o Q = Q o tau holds up to specified natural isomorphisms (equality only for the construction by fractions); the composites with Q are Q(i_q), Q(j_q) up to these.

a : T₀ ≅ G, whiskerLeft Q a.hom ≫ e.hom = e₀.hom) ∧ (∀ (G : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory A) (e : Q ⋙ G ≅ (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntLE q).truncLEFunctor A ⋙ Q), ∃! a : T₁ ≅ G, whiskerLeft Q a.hom ≫ e.hom = e₁.hom) ∧ (∀ (G : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory A) (e : Q ⋙ G ≅ (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) q ⋙ CochainComplex.singleFunctor A q) ⋙ Q), ∃! a : H ≅ G, whiskerLeft Q a.hom ≫ e.hom = eH.hom) ∧ (∃! iD : T₀ ⟶ T₁, whiskerLeft Q iD ≫ e₁.hom = e₀.hom ≫ whiskerRight i Q) ∧ (∃! jD : T₁ ⟶ H, whiskerLeft Q jD ≫ eH.hom = e₁.hom ≫ whiskerRight j Q) ∧ ∃ (iD : T₀ ⟶ T₁) (jD : T₁ ⟶ H), (whiskerLeft Q iD ≫ e₁.hom = e₀.hom ≫ whiskerRight i Q) ∧ (whiskerLeft Q jD ≫ eH.hom = e₁.hom ≫ whiskerRight j Q) ∧ (∀ (K L : DerivedCategory A) (f : K ⟶ L), iD.app K ≫ T₁.map f = T₀.map f ≫ iD.app L ∧ jD.app K ≫ H.map f = T₁.map f ≫ jD.app L) ∧ (∀ (K L : CochainComplex A ℤ) (φ : K ⟶ L), T₀.map (Q.map φ) ≫ e₀.hom.app L = e₀.hom.app K ≫ Q.map (CochainComplex.truncLEMap φ (q - 1)) ∧ T₁.map (Q.map φ) ≫ e₁.hom.app L = e₁.hom.app K ≫ Q.map (CochainComplex.truncLEMap φ q) ∧ H.map (Q.map φ) ≫ eH.hom.app L = eH.hom.app K ≫ Q.map ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor A q).map ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) q).map φ)))
